title: The strategy did not die, the market that paid me left
author: Electronic_Tea_2948
selftext: My strategy did not stop working, the market conditions that were paying me just changed, and I wish I had expected that from day one. I used to believe a strategy either works or it does not, but live trading taught me there is a third option, it worked, but only in one kind of market, and then that market went away. Volatility dropped, Nifty went from trending to chopping sideways, India VIX fell and stayed low, and the same setup that printed money for months suddenly left me with brokerage and slippage, even though not one line of code had broken, because the market I had built the strategy for simply stopped showing up. This is nastier than a bad strategy, because overfitting you can catch and measure, but here the study can be completely correct about a market that is already dead. What changed how I trade was switching the question from whether this works to what has to stay true for this to keep working, and if the honest answer is that VIX has to stay high, or the market has to keep trending, then that is not a side note, that is the real bet. I still do not have a clean way to spot the shift while it is happening, all I have is scars and a shorter leash, so I try to write the required conditions before I put serious money on it, I keep a rule for a rough patch versus genuinely dead, and I try not to keep a losing strategy running only because I still believe the tape is on my side. I am trying to stop using the market changed as an excuse after a loss, and start treating it as part of the plan from the beginning.

comments.author: Fynca
comments.body: The tricky part is deciding when to switch it back on. Otherwise you can end up pausing after the losses and returning after the recovery. Have you figured out what would convince you the right conditions are back?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
The fix for the spotting problem is to make the precondition a number you log daily, not a sentence in a doc. If the bet is that VIX stays high, write the band, then record where it sits each day beside the equity curve.

What helped most was measuring that condition over the backtest window first, so you know what normal looked like in the period that actually paid. When today sits outside that range, the market you built for is gone, and you see it before the drawdown explains it to you.

comments.author: pathtogreatness8
comments.body: That is why filters are important

comments.author: Foreign-Safe-8161
comments.body: *This is one of the most mature realizations on this sub. Most people confuse a broken strategy with a changed market regime. When the structural conditions (like volatility, liquidity profile, or order flow imbalance) shift, your code is technically fine, but your alpha's oxygen supply has been cut off. Shifting the question from 'does it work' to 'what must remain true for this to work' is the exact difference between a retail gambler and a systematic researcher. Respect*
